raw.description:
Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) is responsible for developing, leading and executing the group-wide procurement, strategic sourcing and supplier management strategy across all subsidiaries, business units, operating entities and geographical markets within the organization.

The role provides strategic leadership over procurement governance, commercial negotiations, vendor relationships, cost optimization, third-party risk management, procurement operations and sourcing transformation. The Group CPO ensures procurement activities support the organization's financial performance, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, business continuity and strategic objectives.

Within an Insurance & Investments group, the role oversees procurement of technology, insurance operations, investment-related services, professional services, outsourcing, facilities, corporate services and other strategic goods and services.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Group Procurement Strategy & Leadership

  • Develop and implement the group-wide procurement strategy aligned with corporate objectives, financial targets and business priorities.
  • Establish procurement policies, frameworks, standards and operating models across subsidiaries and business units.
  • Lead centralized, decentralized or hybrid procurement structures to optimize group-wide purchasing activities.
  • Drive procurement maturity, operational efficiency and strategic sourcing capability across the organization.
  • Advise executive leadership and the board on procurement strategy, commercial opportunities and supplier-related risks.

B. Strategic Sourcing & Category Management

  • Lead strategic sourcing initiatives across major procurement categories, including IT, insurance operations, investment services, consulting, outsourcing, facilities and corporate services.
  • Develop category strategies, sourcing plans, supplier selection frameworks and procurement roadmaps.
  • Oversee competitive bidding, RFPs, RFQs, tendering, vendor evaluations and contract award processes.
  • Identify opportunities for group-wide procurement consolidation, economies of scale and supplier rationalization.
  • Drive strategic negotiations to secure commercial value, quality, service delivery and contractual protection.

C. Supplier & Vendor Management

  • Establish and oversee strategic supplier relationship management frameworks across the group.
  • Manage relationships with key suppliers, strategic partners, technology providers, outsourcing partners and service providers.
  • Develop supplier performance management frameworks, service-level agreements (SLAs), scorecards and review mechanisms.
  • Monitor supplier delivery, service quality, financial stability, contractual obligations and operational performance.
  • Lead supplier escalation, renegotiation, remediation and relationship improvement initiatives.

D. Cost Optimization & Financial Management

  • Drive procurement-led savings, cost optimization, cost avoidance and financial efficiency across group operations.
  • Develop procurement budgets, savings targets, spend forecasts and financial reporting frameworks.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize operating expenditure (OPEX), capital expenditure (CAPEX) and vendor spending.
  • Collaborate with Finance, business leaders and subsidiary management to validate procurement savings and benefits realization.
  • Monitor procurement spend, budget performance, financial controls and cost reduction initiatives.

E. Contract & Commercial Management

  • Lead complex commercial negotiations, strategic contract agreements, supplier terms and procurement-related commitments.
  • Establish group-wide contract management standards, renewal controls and commercial governance.
  • Ensure contracts reflect pricing, performance requirements, service levels, risk allocation, termination provisions and business continuity obligations.
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, Risk and Compliance teams on contract review, commercial risk and regulatory obligations.
  • Monitor contract lifecycle management, renewals, variations, disputes and contractual performance.

F. Procurement Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Establish procurement governance frameworks, delegated authority structures, approval processes and procurement controls.
  • Ensure procurement practices comply with regulatory requirements, internal policies, ethical standards and corporate governance.
  • Oversee supplier due diligence, procurement risk assessments, conflict-of-interest controls and supplier integrity checks.
  • Collaborate with Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit and Legal teams to manage procurement-related risks.
  • Ensure procurement transparency, audit readiness, accountability and responsible purchasing practices.

G. Third-Party Risk & Outsourcing Management

  • Lead group-level oversight of third-party relationships, outsourced services and strategic vendor dependencies.
  • Ensure supplier risk assessment, due diligence, onboarding, monitoring and exit management processes are implemented.
  • Manage third-party operational, cybersecurity, data privacy, financial, reputational and business continuity risks.
  • Oversee critical supplier and outsourcing arrangements relevant to insurance and investment operations.
  • Ensure third-party governance aligns with the organization's risk management framework and applicable regulatory expectations.

H. Procurement Transformation & Digitalization

  • Drive procurement transformation initiatives to improve sourcing efficiency, automation, analytics and process standardization.
  • Implement or oversee procurement technology, e-procurement, spend analytics, contract management and supplier management platforms.
  • Leverage data analytics and technology to improve procurement visibility, forecasting, supplier performance and decision-making.
  • Lead process redesign, procurement operating model transformation and digital procurement adoption.
  • Promote continuous improvement, innovation and best practices across the group procurement function.

I. Executive Stakeholder & Business Partnership

  • Partner with Group CEO, COO, CFO, CIO, business unit leaders and subsidiary executives on procurement priorities.
  • Align procurement strategies with business growth, transformation, investment, operational and organizational priorities.
  • Provide executive-level procurement insights, recommendations, performance reports and strategic analysis.
  • Influence senior stakeholders on sourcing decisions, supplier strategy, commercial risk and cost optimization.
  • Build strong cross-functional relationships to ensure procurement delivers business value.

J. Team Leadership & Organizational Development

  • Lead, develop and oversee group procurement, strategic sourcing, category management and vendor management teams.
  • Establish organizational structures, talent development plans, performance expectations and succession strategies.
  • Promote procurement excellence, ethical conduct, accountability, collaboration and commercial awareness.
  • Build procurement capability across subsidiaries, business units and regional operations.
  • Drive leadership development, performance management and continuous professional development.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Finance, Economics or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA), Supply Chain Management, Procurement or Strategic Management preferred.
  • Professional certifications such as CIPS, CPSM, MCIPS or equivalent procurement qualifications are highly desirable.

Professional Experience

  • 12–18+ years of progressive procurement, sourcing, commercial or supply chain experience.
  • Significant experience in senior procurement leadership, preferably at Director, VP or C-suite level.
  • Proven experience leading group-wide, multi-entity, multinational or multi-business procurement functions.
  • Strong experience in strategic sourcing, category management, contract negotiation and supplier management.
  • Demonstrated track record of delivering measurable cost savings, procurement transformation and commercial value.
  • Experience managing procurement across complex organizations, regulated industries or financial services environments.
  • Experience in third-party risk management, outsourcing governance and supplier performance management.
  • Exposure to insurance, investment management, banking, financial services or other highly regulated industries is preferred.

Technical & Leadership Competencies

  • Group-wide procurement strategy and governance.
  • Strategic sourcing and category management.
  • Commercial negotiation and contract management.
  • Supplier relationship and vendor management.
  • Spend analytics and financial management.
  • Third-party risk and outsourcing oversight.
  • Procurement transformation and digitalization.
  • Regulatory compliance and corporate governance.

- Executive stakeholder management.

  • Organizational leadership and team development.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

KPI CategoryPerformance Indicators

Cost SavingsProcurement savings, cost avoidance and cost optimization achieved across the group.

Spend ManagementSpend under management, procurement spend visibility and strategic spend coverage.

Sourcing EffectivenessCompetitive sourcing rates, sourcing cycle time and sourcing strategy execution.

Supplier PerformanceSupplier SLA achievement, quality, delivery performance and supplier scorecard results.

Contract ManagementContract compliance, contract coverage, renewal management and negotiated commercial value.

Procurement CompliancePolicy compliance, approval adherence, audit findings and procurement control effectiveness.

Third-Party RiskSupplier risk assessment completion, critical supplier monitoring and risk remediation.

Operational EfficiencyProcurement cycle time, process efficiency and procurement service delivery.

TransformationProcurement technology adoption, automation and process improvement outcomes.

LeadershipProcurement team performance, capability development, stakeholder satisfaction and succession readiness.

We exist to create positive change for people and the planet. Join us and make a difference too!

Head of Artificial Intelligence Global Quality & Accreditation

Location: Global Homebased, travel required

About the role

We have an exciting opportunity become available for the Head of AI Global Quality & Accreditation. The purpose of this role will be to:

  • Lead BSI’s efforts in Developing Conformity Assessment Activity to allow manufacturers and providers to demonstrate that their technology conforms to the provisions of the evolving EU AI Regulations
  • Be the ambassador representing BSI as a global leader in key AI Technical Forums in Europe and Globally as an industry leading expert regulator.
  • Ensure that NB personnel work consistently at the required high level of expertise and rigour
  • Ensure that BSI has the relevant policies, procedures and documentation are in place to meet all AI regulatory obligations
  • Work with the GRC team on competence qualifications, personal development and certificate decision making. This responsibility will involve the application of personal authority and expertise rather than hierarchical position.
  • Shape & define BSI Group business plan for AI and Machine Learning in the regulatory space, working alongside Marketing and the innovations Team to identify and quantify opportunities in high risk areas with mandated regulation.
  • Possible Focus areas may include:
  • Medical Devices / In vitro Diagnostic Devices
  • Real time/remote biometric identification
  • Equipment and protective systems for use in explosive atmospheres
  • Radio equipment
  • Pressure equipment
  • Appliances burning gaseous fuels
  • Road traffic, supply of water, gas, heating, and electricity

Key responsibilities:

  • Lead the Designation activity to obtain AI Notified Body Status within the EU in the targeted areas and lead on regulatory issues, both internal and external.
  • Lead the development and implementation of the necessary processes and procedures that enable staff to comply with the EU AI Regulation and associated Notified Body designation and accreditation requirements.
  • Work with the GRC Professional Development team to establish qualification criteria for all roles.
  • Lead your team to ensure staff comply with the new AI NB’s processes and procedures working with the GRC Professional Development group.
  • Lead your team in providing expert regulatory support for the wider team (Group) and to customers.
  • Mentor and Support NL Team with Designating Authority (TBC).
  • Support the UK Approved Body and other International Regulatory programs.
  • Identify the opportunities for business process improvement.
  • Keep the Certification Process output consistent working with C&R, Operations, and Professional Development to support all operational teams.

To be successful in the role you will have:

  • BSc degree in discipline relevant to AI and or from a target industry sector. Postgraduate qualification in AI & or Machine learning Technology and or a Regulatory Affairs background would be advantageous.
  • Thorough knowledge of existing and proposed AI regulations worldwide and particularly the EU AI regulatory approach.
  • Knowledge of business processes and the application of quality management standards
  • A team player good at relationship building internally and externally
  • Broad technical understanding of focal area industry products
  • Conceptual and analytical thinking, efficiency, and results orientation
  • General knowledge of business principles and operating practices (commercial awareness)
  • Ability to understand and interpret legislation and input to policy
  • People leadership / influencing skills
  • Good interpersonal skills, particularly communication and influencing skills
  • Capable of operating with horizontal and vertical reporting lines

BSI offers a competitive total reward package, an independent and varied job in an international environment, flexible working hours, ongoing training and development.

The salary for Netherlands can range from €96,000-120,000 annually; actual compensation is based on various factors, including but not limited to, the candidate’s competencies, level of experience, education, location, divisional budget and internal peer compensation comparisons. As this role can be based homebased globally across EMEA your recruiter can advise of salary for the country you are based.

About Us

BSI is a business improvement and standards company and for over a century BSI has been recognized for having a positive impact on organizations and society, building trust and enhancing lives.

Today BSI partners with more than 77,500 clients in 195 countries and engages with a 15,000 strong global community of experts, industry and consumer groups, organizations and governments.
Utilizing its extensive expertise in key industry sectors - including automotive, aerospace, built environment, food and retail, and healthcare - BSI delivers on its purpose by helping its clients fulfil theirs.
Living by our core values of Client-Centricity, Agility, and Collaboration, BSI provides organizations with the confidence to grow by partnering with them to tackle society’s critical issues – from climate change to building trust in digital transformation and everything in between - to accelerate progress towards a better society and a sustainable world.

BSI is an Equal Opportunity Employer dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace.

Customer Service Representative (CSR)

Customer Support | Phone, Email & Live Chat | Remote Support

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Client Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Customer Service Representative (CSR) to deliver fast, professional, and empathetic customer support across phone, email, live chat, and ticketing systems.

This is a customer-facing support role designed for someone who thrives in fast-paced environments, communicates clearly under pressure, and genuinely enjoys helping customers solve problems.

You will serve as the frontline voice of the company, ensuring customers receive timely support, accurate resolutions, and an exceptional experience throughout every interaction.

If you’re calm under pressure, organized, solutions-oriented, and committed to delivering outstanding customer service, this role is a great fit.

What You’ll Own

Customer Support & Issue Resolution

  • Respond to inbound customer inquiries via:
    • Phone
    • Email
    • Live Chat
    • Support Tickets
  • Resolve customer concerns professionally and efficiently.
  • Troubleshoot common issues and escalate complex cases when appropriate.
  • Deliver positive customer experiences that build trust and satisfaction.
  • Balance multiple conversations while maintaining high service quality.

Ticket & Case Management

  • Manage support requests using platforms such as:
    • Zendesk
    • Freshdesk
    • Help Scout
    • Salesforce Service Cloud
  • Prioritize tickets based on urgency and service-level agreements (SLAs).
  • Document customer interactions accurately within support systems.
  • Monitor open cases and ensure timely follow-up through resolution.
  • Maintain organized and audit-ready customer support records.

Customer Experience & Communication

  • Communicate professionally and empathetically across all channels.
  • De-escalate challenging customer situations with patience and professionalism.
  • Maintain a customer-first mindset throughout every interaction.
  • Capture customer feedback and identify recurring issues.
  • Ensure customers remain informed throughout the resolution process.

Knowledge Base & Process Improvement

  • Update FAQs, knowledge base articles, and response templates.
  • Improve support macros and communication workflows.
  • Identify recurring issues and recommend process improvements.
  • Share customer insights with internal teams to improve overall service quality.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with:
    • Operations
    • Billing
    • Technical Support
    • Product Teams
  • Coordinate escalations efficiently.
  • Follow company procedures, documentation standards, and privacy policies.

Requirements

Must-Have Qualifications

Experience

  • 1–2+ years of experience in:
    • Customer Service
    • Customer Support
    • Call Center
    • Client-Facing Support

Technical Skills

  • Experience using customer support platforms such as:
    • Zendesk
    • Freshdesk
    • Help Scout
    • Salesforce Service Cloud
  • Proficiency with:
    • Google Workspace
    • Microsoft Office
  • Comfortable working in high-volume customer support environments.
  • Reliable internet connection and professional remote workspace.

Communication Skills

  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Professional, empathetic, and customer-focused communication style.
  • Strong multitasking and organizational abilities.
  • Ability to manage difficult customer situations with professionalism.

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience supporting U.S.-based customers.
  • Background in:
    • SaaS
    • E-commerce
    • Healthcare
    • Finance
    • Service-Based Businesses
  • Experience working in KPI-driven support environments.
  • Familiarity with:
    • Live Chat Systems
    • Support Automation Tools
  • Multilingual communication skills.

Tools & Platforms

  • Zendesk
  • Freshdesk
  • Help Scout
  • Salesforce Service Cloud
  • Google Workspace
  • Microsoft Office
  • Live Chat & Ticketing Platforms

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You genuinely enjoy helping customers solve problems.
  • You remain calm and professional under pressure.
  • You communicate clearly across phone, email, and chat.
  • You can manage high ticket volumes without sacrificing quality.
  • You’re organized, detail-oriented, and reliable.
  • You take ownership of customer concerns until they are fully resolved.

What a Typical Day Looks Like

  • Review and prioritize inbound customer inquiries.
  • Respond to customers via phone, email, and live chat.
  • Troubleshoot issues and coordinate escalations when needed.
  • Update ticketing systems with accurate notes and documentation.
  • Follow up on unresolved cases until completion.
  • Identify recurring customer issues and suggest improvements.

In short: You provide fast, professional, and solutions-focused customer support that strengthens customer satisfaction and long-term loyalty.

Key Metrics for Success (KPIs)

  • First Contact Resolution (FCR)
  • Customer Satisfaction (CSAT)
  • Net Promoter Score (NPS)
  • Average Response Time
  • SLA Compliance
  • Ticket Resolution Time
  • Documentation Accuracy
  • Quality Assurance (QA) Scores

Why Join Us?

  • Fully remote opportunity with U.S. business hours.
  • Make a direct impact on customer experience and retention.
  • Collaborative, supportive, and structured work environment.
  • Work with modern customer support platforms and tools.
  • Career growth opportunities into:
    • Customer Success Specialist
    • Team Lead
    • Operations Support
    • Client Experience Manager

Interview Process

  1. Initial Phone Screen
  2. Spark Hire Intro Video (3–5 minutes)
  3. Practical Assessment (Customer Support Scenarios / Simulated Tickets)
  4. Client Interview
  5. Offer & Background Verification

What Happens After You Apply

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. This short, self-recorded video is the next step that completes your application and can be recorded whenever it’s convenient for you.

Instead of repeating yourself across multiple screening calls, you’ll introduce yourself once, and your video will be shared with the hiring team. This helps the hiring team evaluate your communication style early, making future interviews more meaningful while reducing unnecessary interview rounds.

Don’t overthink it—you can record your video as many times as you’d like before submitting it. Only your final submission will be reviewed.

Please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for your Spark Hire invitation after submitting your application.

Apply Now

If you’re an experienced Customer Service Representative who enjoys helping people, solving problems, and delivering exceptional customer experiences, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today and become a valued part of a growing remote support team where your communication, professionalism, and customer-first mindset will make a real impact.

raw.description:
We're looking for a Senior level GIS Analyst with strong programming skills and a passion for delivering impactful projects. You'll work with a collaborative team to analyze spatial data and build modern web GIS applications that directly serve our clients and their global missions. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable working independently and alongside others, and is driven to continuously learn and share knowledge.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the architecture of Python based data pipelines, setting standards for automation, cleaning, transformation, and analysis of geospatial datasets across projects.
  • Develop ArcGIS Online Hosted Notebooks, ArcGIS Pro Python Toolboxes, and ArcGIS Geoprocessing services to support geospatial applications and workflows
  • Lead database architecture decisions for enterprise relational and spatial systems, balancing performance, scalability, and maintainability.
  • Deliver production-quality code following professional development standards, including version control with Git and GitHub for collaboration, collaborative code review, and release management
  • Perform quality assurance and debugging of geospatial data, scripts, and services to ensure accuracy, performance, and reliability of delivered solutions
  • Give live demonstrations and presentations to clients showcasing workflows, solutions, and outcomes
  • Collaborate with clients to define project requirements, translate business needs into technical specifications, and communicate progress throughout the project lifecycle
  • Serve as technical lead on select engagements, guiding architecture and implementation approach
  • Mentor junior analysts and foster knowledge-sharing across the team

Requirements

  • 8+ years of professional GIS experience
  • Advanced proficiency across the Esri stack: ArcGIS Pro (with extensions), ArcGIS Online, and ArcGIS Enterprise (Server, Portal, Image Server)
  • Demonstrated Python 3.x development experience building complex, production-ready geospatial tools; proficiency with ArcPy, ArcGIS API for Python, NumPy, and Pandas at minimum
  • Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent projects, proactively identify risks, and communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders in a client-facing environment

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours

About the Role

We are looking for a detail-oriented Medical Billing Specialist to manage the day-to-day medical billing and claims process for Carson Day. This role will focus on accurate claims submission, payment posting, denial management, and accounts receivable follow-up to ensure timely reimbursements and minimize billing errors.

The ideal candidate has hands-on medical billing experience, understands insurance claims and coding requirements, and can independently manage billing workflows while keeping the Finance team informed of progress and outstanding issues.

What You'll Own

1. Claims Submission & Management

  • Prepare, review, and submit accurate medical claims to insurance payers.
  • Ensure claims meet applicable coding, documentation, and payer requirements.
  • Monitor claim statuses and address errors or submission issues promptly.

2. Payment Posting & Reconciliation

  • Post insurance payments, adjustments, and denials accurately to patient accounts.
  • Review Explanation of Benefits (EOBs) and reconcile payments against expected reimbursements.
  • Identify and investigate payment discrepancies.

3. Denial Management

  • Investigate denied and rejected claims to identify the root causes.
  • Prepare and submit corrected claims or appeals within required deadlines.
  • Track denial patterns and follow up to ensure outstanding issues are resolved.

4. Accounts Receivable & Follow-Up

  • Monitor outstanding balances and follow up on unpaid or pending claims.
  • Contact insurance carriers to resolve payment delays and billing discrepancies.
  • Track aging accounts and escalate outstanding issues when necessary.

5. Patient & Payer Communication

  • Respond to billing-related inquiries from patients and insurance representatives.
  • Communicate professionally to resolve claim discrepancies and payment-related concerns.
  • Keep the Finance team updated on progress, outstanding items, and potential blockers.

6. Accuracy & Compliance

  • Maintain accurate billing records and documentation.
  • Follow applicable healthcare billing regulations, payer guidelines, and internal Finance procedures.
  • Handle patient and payer information with strict confidentiality.

Requirements

  • Proven experience in medical billing, claims processing, or a closely related healthcare finance role.
  • Solid understanding of medical coding systems, including ICD-10, CPT, and HCPCS.
  • Familiarity with insurance verification, EOBs, and payment remittance processing.
  • Hands-on experience using medical billing software or practice management systems.
  • Understanding of the complete claims lifecycle, from submission through payment and follow-up.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to identify and resolve billing discrepancies.
  • Excellent written and spoken English communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and manage daily billing tasks in a remote environment.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You take ownership of assigned billing tasks and follow through without constant supervision.
  • You proactively identify discrepancies and resolve issues before they affect collections.
  • You are organized and consistent when handling repetitive, detail-oriented work.
  • You communicate clearly with the Finance team and external insurance representatives.
  • You understand the importance of accuracy, confidentiality, and timely follow-up in medical billing.

What Success Looks Like

  • Claims are submitted accurately and within required deadlines.
  • Payments are posted and reconciled consistently.
  • Denials are investigated and resolved promptly.
  • Outstanding AR balances receive timely follow-up.
  • Billing discrepancies are identified and addressed before they cause delays.
  • The Finance team has clear visibility into billing progress and outstanding issues.

  • Initial Recruiter Interview
  • Client Interview
  • Offer & Onbaording

About CG Oncology, Inc.

Are you ready to make a difference in the world and become part of our patient-centered team that is focused on Attacking Bladder Cancer for a Better Tomorrow? At CG Oncology, we believe that by having exceptionally talented individuals on our team who share our passion and enjoy working together, we can truly achieve our Vision and Mission to benefit patients around the world.

Every day we are making significant advancements across our multiple pipelines and are growing rapidly to meet the needs of our patients who cannot afford to wait to benefit from our novel immunotherapies. Please review this job posting and our Values and if they resonate with you and are what you expect from your organization and team, then we would like to hear from you.

About the role

CG Oncology is seeking a director of HCP marketing to co-design and co-lead our healthcare professional (HCP) marketing strategy and execution for cretostimogene across the pre-launch, launch and post-launch lifecycle.

This individual will build a comprehensive physician-to-physician engagement strategy designed to educate urologists and other appropriate healthcare professionals on the evolving NMIBC treatment landscape, appropriate patient identification, and the potential role of cretostimogene.

This individual will translate clinical evidence, customer insights and market dynamics into differentiated positioning, compelling HCP messaging, effective promotional resources and launch plans. The Director will partner closely with co-HCP Marketing, Medical Affairs, Market Access, Patient Marketing, Peer-to-Peer Marketing and Customer Experience Marketing to support pre-launch readiness, launch execution and ongoing brand performance. The role requires strong clinical acumen, strategic marketing judgment and hands-on execution in a regulated environment. The role will initially focus on high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC while building the capabilities and insights required to support potential future indications, including intermediate-risk NMIBC.

Essential Functions

HCP Brand Strategy

  • Jointly develop the HCP marketing plan, including customer priorities, strategic imperatives, tactical initiatives and resource allocation
  • Develop and refine HCP positioning, value propositions, messaging flow, based on clinical evidence, market research and competitive dynamics.
  • Coordinate with Medical Affairs team to develop core brand strategies and appropriate data dissemination strategies

Insights Development and Brand Management

  • Partner with Market Research and Insights to design insight-generation plans, monitor customer feedback and evaluate HCP marketing promotional response
  • Generate a core set of HCP marketing KPIs, including message awareness, adoption and utilization across core segments
  • Manage assigned HCP marketing budgets, agency deliverables, contracts and forecasts with financial discipline.
  • Lead agency partners and cross-functional project teams to deliver high-quality work on time and within budget.

Promotional Execution

  • Co-lead strategy, development and lifecycle management of HCP promotional materials, including core visual aids, clinical data resources and non-personal assets
  • Work to ensure all tactics are consistent with overall brand strategy and aligned with Medical, Legal and Regulatory standards
  • Partner with co-HCP marketing, Customer Experience, and Peer to Peer marketing to align all strategies across the brand

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in marketing, business administration or a related field or equivalent years of experience required. MBA or other graduate degree preferred.
  • Ten (10+) years pharmaceutical or biotech commercialization experience.
  • Experience working in pharmaceutical brand marketing, urology preferred.
  • Significant experience in pharmaceutical marketing, with direct experience leading peer-to-peer or HCP marketing programs.
  • Oncology experience strongly preferred; urology, bladder cancer or physician-administered oncology experience highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting a pharmaceutical product launch.
  • Experience developing and managing commercial speaker bureaus and peer-to-peer programs.
  • Strong understanding of HCP segmentation, targeting and customer engagement.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate effectively within Regulatory, Legal and Compliance requirements.
  • Up to 20-25% travel required
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, social media platforms, and communication technology tools.

Work Authorization for US Applicants:Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

Please note that CG Oncology does not accept unsolicited information and/or resumes from search firms or agencies for our job postings. Any resumes or client information submitted to our careers page or any employee of CG Oncology by any search firm or agency without an applicable contract in place will become the property of CG Oncology and no fee(s) will be paid.

Total Rewards

CG Oncology offers very competitive and comprehensive Total Rewards, helping to support and reward our global team of high-performing employees focused on developing bladder-saving therapeutics for patients afflicted with bladder cancer.

HIGHLY COMPETITIVE SALARIES

ANNUAL PERFORMANCE/MERIT REVIEWS

ANNUAL PERFORMANCE BONUSES

EQUITYSPECIAL RECOGNITION

Well-Being Benefits

In addition to our Total Rewards, CG Oncology offers a variety of Well-Being Benefits to meet the majority of the needs of our unique and growing workforce. These benefits are designed to support our team to achieve a healthy balance between work and their personal lives to remain refreshed, engaged, and creating an environment where each person can find a deeper meaning and purpose in their work.

Well-Being Benefits eligibility begins the 1st of the month after hire. While a majority of these benefits are for our US-based workforce, we continue to assess comparable levels of benefits for our international team members that are aligned with country-specific regulations and their national programs offered.

FULLY REMOTE WORK ENVIRONMENT

REST AND RECHARGE BENEFITS - Unlimited Flexible Time Off

HOLIDAYS - In 2026 we will observe 14 holidays

ADDITIONAL EXCLUSIVE BENEFITS - Voluntary Legal, Pet, Plus More

CG Oncology is an Equal Opportunity Employer:

All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status. At CG Oncology, we are building a community of intelligent and passionate team members that share our Vision, Mission and Values, and while the biotechnology space can feel limited in BIPOC, non-binary and even female representation, we endeavor to make hiring decisions that will continue to grow and support our team in the direction of maintaining cultural diversity and sustainability.

Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) is responsible for developing, leading and executing the group-wide procurement, strategic sourcing and supplier management strategy across all subsidiaries, business units, operating entities and geographical markets within the organization.

The role provides strategic leadership over procurement governance, commercial negotiations, vendor relationships, cost optimization, third-party risk management, procurement operations and sourcing transformation. The Group CPO ensures procurement activities support the organization's financial performance, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, business continuity and strategic objectives.

Within an Insurance & Investments group, the role oversees procurement of technology, insurance operations, investment-related services, professional services, outsourcing, facilities, corporate services and other strategic goods and services.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Group Procurement Strategy & Leadership

  • Develop and implement the group-wide procurement strategy aligned with corporate objectives, financial targets and business priorities.
  • Establish procurement policies, frameworks, standards and operating models across subsidiaries and business units.
  • Lead centralized, decentralized or hybrid procurement structures to optimize group-wide purchasing activities.
  • Drive procurement maturity, operational efficiency and strategic sourcing capability across the organization.
  • Advise executive leadership and the board on procurement strategy, commercial opportunities and supplier-related risks.

B. Strategic Sourcing & Category Management

  • Lead strategic sourcing initiatives across major procurement categories, including IT, insurance operations, investment services, consulting, outsourcing, facilities and corporate services.
  • Develop category strategies, sourcing plans, supplier selection frameworks and procurement roadmaps.
  • Oversee competitive bidding, RFPs, RFQs, tendering, vendor evaluations and contract award processes.
  • Identify opportunities for group-wide procurement consolidation, economies of scale and supplier rationalization.
  • Drive strategic negotiations to secure commercial value, quality, service delivery and contractual protection.

C. Supplier & Vendor Management

  • Establish and oversee strategic supplier relationship management frameworks across the group.
  • Manage relationships with key suppliers, strategic partners, technology providers, outsourcing partners and service providers.
  • Develop supplier performance management frameworks, service-level agreements (SLAs), scorecards and review mechanisms.
  • Monitor supplier delivery, service quality, financial stability, contractual obligations and operational performance.
  • Lead supplier escalation, renegotiation, remediation and relationship improvement initiatives.

D. Cost Optimization & Financial Management

  • Drive procurement-led savings, cost optimization, cost avoidance and financial efficiency across group operations.
  • Develop procurement budgets, savings targets, spend forecasts and financial reporting frameworks.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize operating expenditure (OPEX), capital expenditure (CAPEX) and vendor spending.
  • Collaborate with Finance, business leaders and subsidiary management to validate procurement savings and benefits realization.
  • Monitor procurement spend, budget performance, financial controls and cost reduction initiatives.

E. Contract & Commercial Management

  • Lead complex commercial negotiations, strategic contract agreements, supplier terms and procurement-related commitments.
  • Establish group-wide contract management standards, renewal controls and commercial governance.
  • Ensure contracts reflect pricing, performance requirements, service levels, risk allocation, termination provisions and business continuity obligations.
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, Risk and Compliance teams on contract review, commercial risk and regulatory obligations.
  • Monitor contract lifecycle management, renewals, variations, disputes and contractual performance.

F. Procurement Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Establish procurement governance frameworks, delegated authority structures, approval processes and procurement controls.
  • Ensure procurement practices comply with regulatory requirements, internal policies, ethical standards and corporate governance.
  • Oversee supplier due diligence, procurement risk assessments, conflict-of-interest controls and supplier integrity checks.
  • Collaborate with Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit and Legal teams to manage procurement-related risks.
  • Ensure procurement transparency, audit readiness, accountability and responsible purchasing practices.

G. Third-Party Risk & Outsourcing Management

  • Lead group-level oversight of third-party relationships, outsourced services and strategic vendor dependencies.
  • Ensure supplier risk assessment, due diligence, onboarding, monitoring and exit management processes are implemented.
  • Manage third-party operational, cybersecurity, data privacy, financial, reputational and business continuity risks.
  • Oversee critical supplier and outsourcing arrangements relevant to insurance and investment operations.
  • Ensure third-party governance aligns with the organization's risk management framework and applicable regulatory expectations.

H. Procurement Transformation & Digitalization

  • Drive procurement transformation initiatives to improve sourcing efficiency, automation, analytics and process standardization.
  • Implement or oversee procurement technology, e-procurement, spend analytics, contract management and supplier management platforms.
  • Leverage data analytics and technology to improve procurement visibility, forecasting, supplier performance and decision-making.
  • Lead process redesign, procurement operating model transformation and digital procurement adoption.
  • Promote continuous improvement, innovation and best practices across the group procurement function.

I. Executive Stakeholder & Business Partnership

  • Partner with Group CEO, COO, CFO, CIO, business unit leaders and subsidiary executives on procurement priorities.
  • Align procurement strategies with business growth, transformation, investment, operational and organizational priorities.
  • Provide executive-level procurement insights, recommendations, performance reports and strategic analysis.
  • Influence senior stakeholders on sourcing decisions, supplier strategy, commercial risk and cost optimization.
  • Build strong cross-functional relationships to ensure procurement delivers business value.

J. Team Leadership & Organizational Development

  • Lead, develop and oversee group procurement, strategic sourcing, category management and vendor management teams.
  • Establish organizational structures, talent development plans, performance expectations and succession strategies.
  • Promote procurement excellence, ethical conduct, accountability, collaboration and commercial awareness.
  • Build procurement capability across subsidiaries, business units and regional operations.
  • Drive leadership development, performance management and continuous professional development.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Finance, Economics or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA), Supply Chain Management, Procurement or Strategic Management preferred.
  • Professional certifications such as CIPS, CPSM, MCIPS or equivalent procurement qualifications are highly desirable.

Professional Experience

  • 12–18+ years of progressive procurement, sourcing, commercial or supply chain experience.
  • Significant experience in senior procurement leadership, preferably at Director, VP or C-suite level.
  • Proven experience leading group-wide, multi-entity, multinational or multi-business procurement functions.
  • Strong experience in strategic sourcing, category management, contract negotiation and supplier management.
  • Demonstrated track record of delivering measurable cost savings, procurement transformation and commercial value.
  • Experience managing procurement across complex organizations, regulated industries or financial services environments.
  • Experience in third-party risk management, outsourcing governance and supplier performance management.
  • Exposure to insurance, investment management, banking, financial services or other highly regulated industries is preferred.

Technical & Leadership Competencies

  • Group-wide procurement strategy and governance.
  • Strategic sourcing and category management.
  • Commercial negotiation and contract management.
  • Supplier relationship and vendor management.
  • Spend analytics and financial management.
  • Third-party risk and outsourcing oversight.
  • Procurement transformation and digitalization.
  • Regulatory compliance and corporate governance.

- Executive stakeholder management.

  • Organizational leadership and team development.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

KPI CategoryPerformance Indicators

Cost SavingsProcurement savings, cost avoidance and cost optimization achieved across the group.

Spend ManagementSpend under management, procurement spend visibility and strategic spend coverage.

Sourcing EffectivenessCompetitive sourcing rates, sourcing cycle time and sourcing strategy execution.

Supplier PerformanceSupplier SLA achievement, quality, delivery performance and supplier scorecard results.

Contract ManagementContract compliance, contract coverage, renewal management and negotiated commercial value.

Procurement CompliancePolicy compliance, approval adherence, audit findings and procurement control effectiveness.

Third-Party RiskSupplier risk assessment completion, critical supplier monitoring and risk remediation.

Operational EfficiencyProcurement cycle time, process efficiency and procurement service delivery.

TransformationProcurement technology adoption, automation and process improvement outcomes.

LeadershipProcurement team performance, capability development, stakeholder satisfaction and succession readiness.

Overview

Marketing Manager- Enterprise

About the role:

McGraw Hill Higher Education is seeking a Marketing Manager to help plan and execute campaigns and field marketing programs for our enterprise solutions and services.

Reporting to the Director, Enterprise B2B Marketing, this person will help connect institutional leaders with relevant solutions through targeted campaigns, conferences, webinars, and account-focused outreach. They will work closely with enterprise sales and product marketing to translate institutional needs and sales priorities into coordinated marketing activities that build awareness, generate qualified interest, and support opportunity development.

This role is well suited to someone with marketing experience or a sales background who understands customer needs, builds strong partnerships, and demonstrates the ability to learn and apply marketing practices.

What you will do:

  • Plan and execute integrated campaigns aligned with Enterprise priorities, including new solution launches, managing audiences, timelines, deliverables, and follow-up in partnership with product marketing and sales.
  • Understand priority accounts and sales objectives. Develop targeted outreach and programs that engage institutional stakeholders, generate qualified meetings, and support opportunity development.
  • Build knowledge of decisionmakers, institutional needs, buying processes, and use cases to inform campaign targeting and execution.
  • Coordinate conferences, regional events, VIP events, and account-specific events, including agenda development, engagement strategies, attendee participation, and post-event follow-up. .
  • Collaborate with product marketing to apply approved messaging and adapt existing resources for specific audiences, campaigns, and sales outreach.
  • Coordinate with sales and marketing operations on lead routing, timely follow-up, and nurture activities based on expressed interests and institutional needs.
  • Track leads, customer engagement, qualified meetings, and campaign contribution to pipeline; use findings to refine targeting, messaging, and execution.

We’re looking for someone with:

  • Bachelor's Degree required.
  • Proficiency with Salesforce and Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Ability to travel up to 30%
  • Relevant experience in marketing, sales, account management, or a related customer-facing role.
  • An understanding of how sales teams build relationships, identify needs, and develop opportunities.
  • Experience executing campaigns or events, or demonstrated aptitude and willingness to learn audience targeting, campaign planning, nurture, and measurement.
  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills.
  • Strong writing and communication skills, with the ability to adapt messaging to different audiences.
  • Strong project management skills and the ability to coordinate multiple initiatives across teams.
  • A collaborative approach and the ability to move work forward independently

Why work for us?

At McGraw-Hill, we leverage cutting-edge technology to create innovative learning solutions that support learners at all stages of their educational journey. Our state-of-the-art digital tools and platforms provide personalized, interactive experiences that enhance understanding and retention. Being part of McGraw-Hill means joining a team dedicated to shaping the future of education and making a real impact on students' lives. It's an exciting opportunity to contribute to a company that values innovation, collaboration, and excellence.

The pay range for this position is between $80,000 - $107,000 annually. However, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and location. raw.description:
Who We Are

Spectro Cloud helps platform teams and cloud providers modernize and manage infrastructure for the AI era without adding more tools or operational complexity.
With PaletteAI, enterprises, public sector organizations, neoclouds and sovereign clouds can build, govern and operate full-stack environments across VMs, Kubernetes, edge, regulated and air-gapped locations, and AI infrastructure. PaletteAI Launchpads help teams start quickly with urgent outcomes such as VMware migration, token cost control or edge modernization, then scale into enterprise-wide lifecycle management, governance and fleet operations on the same platform.

About The Team

The Partner Enablement Manager builds the partner-specific content that gets partner sellers and engineers selling and delivering Spectro Cloud, including AI. This person speaks partner sales (margin, rebates, deal registration, co-sell, services attach) and writes accurate technical material, then uses AI to turn a partner request into a usable asset in days, not weeks. They also own the certification framework that sits underneath it.

What You’ll Do

Bespoke partner content (~35%)

  • Build partner-specific kits for priority partners and the three customer plays (AI, Edge, Modern Infrastructure): positioning, one-pagers, battlecards, talk tracks, discovery guides, demo flows, lab guides, and short e-learning. Start from approved core assets and tailor them to the partner's value proposition, customer use case, and sales motion. Use AI to draft fast, then get technical review from SEs and Product and messaging approval from Marketing before anything ships. Keep a versioned library by use case in Allbound. Build AI roleplays so partner reps rehearse conversations before they meet customers.

Partner field engagement and iteration (~20%)

  • Run working sessions with partner sales and SE teams, in person and virtual, including pilots such as the Arrow session. Join live partner engagements, capture the questions partners ask and where deals stall, and update kits within days. Translate between Product and partner sellers in both directions. Send gaps back to Product, Marketing, and Channel.

Certification framework (~25%)

  • Own the Sales and Tech tracks across Tier 1 (Associate), Tier 2 (Professional), and Tier 3 (Expert). Start Tier 2 specialist paths with Instinct Coder, then add paths such as VMware modernization, token cost control, and AI factories. Scope labs with the Technical team. Run Tier 3 case-study reviews and Delivery Readiness Assessments with Doug. Keep content current with the 24-month recertification cycle and the quarterly content audit. Manage the certification platform (Spectro U), including the Flockjay to Moodle move.

AI-powered program ops (~20%)

  • Automate certification tracking, tier reporting, and eligibility checks across the LMS, Allbound, and Salesforce. Own the rules for individual certification SPIFFs and the Launchpad, Ascent, and Orbital tiers, and hand payout administration to Channel Operations. Support partner program design once margin, rebate, pricing, and tier decisions are final. Report time saved and share what works with the wider Enablement team.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5+ years in partner enablement, channel marketing, partner sales engineering, or channel sales in B2B tech.
  • Fluent in partner sales: deal registration, margin and rebates, MDF, co-sell, services attach, and tiering. Credible in a partner QBR.
  • Hands-on builder of technical content: decks, battlecards, lab guides, demo scripts, and e-learning that SEs and Product sign off on.
  • Working knowledge of Kubernetes, cloud, and virtualization, and of how AI is deployed and run (GPUs, inference, data center to edge).
  • Daily use of AI assistants and agents (for example Claude, ChatGPT, or Copilot) to build content, analyze data, and automate work. Has built prompts, projects, or agents that other people use.
  • A repeatable method for checking AI-generated technical content against product docs and SMEs before it reaches a partner.
  • Curriculum and certification design, including assessments and labs.
  • Experience with an LMS (Moodle preferred, including SCORM, SSO, and badging).
  • Program management across many owners, comfortable with spreadsheets, dashboards, and tracking systems.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Allbound, Salesforce, or another partner relationship management tool.
  • Partner economics and SPIFF design.
  • GTM work with GPU and OEM ecosystems (NVIDIA, AMD, Supermicro, Dell).
  • Public sector or federal partner exposure (VerteX, DDIL, air-gap).
  • Video, courseware, or e-course production.

Construir um ambiente diverso, inclusivo e comprometido com a equidade faz parte do nosso DNA. Entendemos que diversidade, equidade e inclusão são essenciais para criarmos um ambiente seguro com entregas inovadoras e eficientes para nossas pessoas e sociedade.

raw.title: Head of Payments & Payment Strategy
raw.excerpt: We are looking for a Head of Payments who has run payments from the merchant's seat.
raw.description:
We are looking for a Head of Payments who has run payments from the merchant's seat. You have owned checkout, billing and fraud for a global online business, and you were accountable for the revenue those decisions produced.

You will own how our customers pay in every market we sell in: what the payment page looks like, which methods and currencies it offers by region, how transactions are routed and retried, and where we set the line on fraud. Success is measured in checkout conversion, approval rates, recovered revenue, fraud losses and cost per transaction.

This is a hands-on operating role. You will be in the data every day, finding where approvals drop or customers abandon, and fixing it with Product, Engineering, Finance and Risk.
You will work closely with CentroBill, our internal billing and acquiring arm. CentroBill provides the gateway, acquiring relationships and payment method coverage. You are its merchant-side counterpart: you set the requirements, review performance together and push for the routing, coverage and commercial terms the business needs.

About Us

Centro is an international product company with over 20 years of expertise in product development, affiliate marketing and online technologies. Our team of 300+ professionals across Europe and North America builds products used by millions of users worldwide.

What You Will Manage Daily

  • Checkout conversion by market, device, traffic source and product, from payment page load to successful charge.
  • Approval and decline rates by region, acquirer, card type and issuer, split by initial sales, trial conversions, upsells and renewals.
  • Decline reason codes, and the routing, cascading and retry rules that respond to them.
  • Payment method and currency mix in each region, so customers see the options they trust and expect locally.
  • Fraud rules and 3DS settings, watching false declines as closely as fraud losses.
  • Chargebacks, pre-dispute alerts and refunds, tracked against card scheme monitoring thresholds.
  • Recurring billing health: renewal success, failed rebills, retry schedules and involuntary churn.
  • CentroBill and provider performance: uptime, incidents, cost and the fallback when something underperforms.

Key Responsibilities

Checkout and payment page optimization

  • Own the payment page experience across web and mobile: layout, form fields, method ordering, error messaging and localization.
  • Add and tune express checkout options such as Apple Pay and Google Pay where they lift conversion.
  • Run a continuous testing program on checkout flows and report results in conversion and revenue terms.
  • Work with Product and Engineering to prioritize and ship checkout and billing improvements.

Regional payment strategy

  • Decide which cards, wallets, bank transfers and local payment methods to offer in each market, based on customer behavior and unit economics.
  • Set currency, pricing presentation and local acquiring strategy by region to lift approval rates and reduce cross-border costs.
  • Launch payments in new markets and retire methods that do not earn their place.

Authorization and revenue optimization

raw.description:
Zelh is seeking an experienced Trucking Dispatcher to support its growing fleet and help keep trucks loaded, moving, and profitable across the United States. The ideal candidate will have at least one year of hands-on experience dispatching trucks in the U.S. transportation market and will be comfortable managing the complete day-to-day movement of assigned trucks. This includes communicating directly with drivers, coordinating pickups and deliveries, resolving operational issues, and actively searching for loads to minimize empty miles and maximize truck utilization.

This is a proactive position. We are looking for someone who understands that successful dispatching is not simply monitoring trucks—the goal is to consistently find quality freight and keep drivers moving.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage and dispatch assigned trucks across East Coast, West Coast, and nationwide lanes.

  • Maintain consistent communication with drivers regarding load assignments, pickup and delivery times, routes, delays, and operational issues.

  • Actively search load boards and other available sources for freight that fits each truck's location, equipment, schedule, and desired lanes.

  • Negotiate rates with freight brokers and work to secure profitable loads.

  • Minimize deadhead and empty miles by planning ahead and identifying the next load before the current load is completed whenever possible.

  • Coordinate pickups and deliveries and ensure drivers have all necessary load information and documentation.

  • Track trucks and shipments throughout transit and proactively communicate delays or service issues.

  • Build and maintain relationships with brokers and other transportation partners.

  • Understand regional freight markets and recognize strong and weak lanes.

  • Assist drivers with issues that arise while under load and work quickly to find solutions.

  • Maintain accurate load, driver, rate, and operational information.

  • Work closely with Brothers Freight leadership to maximize fleet utilization, service levels, and profitability.

Working conditions:

  • Work schedule: Monday - Friday 8 am- 5 pm EST

  • Competitive Salary in USD

  • Remote mode of work

  • 10+ business days of paid time off

  • Team building and corporate events

  • Equipment provided

  • A supportive team

Requirements

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum of 1 year of experience as a dispatcher within the U.S. trucking industry.

  • Experience actively finding and booking loads, not solely tracking existing shipments.

  • Strong understanding of U.S. geography, freight lanes, and trucking operations.

  • Experience using load boards such as DAT, Truckstop, or similar platforms.

  • Ability to communicate professionally and confidently with drivers and freight brokers.

  • Experience negotiating freight rates is strongly preferred.

  • Ability to manage multiple trucks and priorities simultaneously.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to react quickly when loads, appointments, or driver schedules change.

  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills.

  • Comfortable working independently and taking ownership of assigned trucks.

What Success Looks Like

A successful Brothers Freight dispatcher takes ownership of their assigned trucks from beginning to end. They know where their drivers are, what load they are currently running, when they will become available, and ideally what load they are running next. The objective is simple: keep the trucks loaded, minimize empty miles, communicate with the drivers, provide excellent service, and keep the operation moving profitably.

raw.description:
About Sardina Systems

Sardina Systems builds cloud infrastructure software based on OpenStack, Kubernetes, and Ceph for cloud operators, enterprises, and service providers across the globe. Behind our technology is a distributed team of builders creating reliable systems for our users.

Position summary

Build and operate a live kernel patching feed for AlmaLinux 10. You own the full technical chain, from CVE triage to signed, tested RPMs published in a public repository. This is a hands-on kernel engineering role, not a management or release-coordination position.

Core responsibilities

Patch engineering

  • Track AlmaLinux security advisories (ALSA) and upstream kernel CVEs.
  • Triage CVEs against the published scope: critical, remotely exploitable or actively exploited vulnerabilities.
  • Backport security fixes to the supported AlmaLinux 10 kernels, resolving conflicts across version differences.
  • Generate live patch modules with klp-build. Initially, publish individual CVE patches; evaluate cumulative/atomic replace strategies as the pipeline matures.
  • Identify CVEs that cannot be live patched (e.g. __init changes, data structure layout changes) and record them in the coverage-gap log.

Build and distribution pipeline

  • Reproduce AlmaLinux kernel builds exactly (same source, config and compiler), e.g. in mock with the AlmaLinux buildroot, so modules match the running kernel.
  • Maintain the automated pipeline: CVE scan, build plan, klp-build, RPM packaging, signing, test gate, createrepo_c publication.
  • Plan and execute the move of support to new AlmaLinux kernel releases as they ship.
  • Verify the exact client-side commands work on stock AlmaLinux 10 (dnf kpatch auto plus kpatch-patch-* packages).

Testing and release gate

  • Run the mandatory pre-publication gate on every patch:
  • load and unload on the target kernel in QEMU;

- run kernel livepatch selftests;

  • for high-severity CVEs: apply and revert under load on a FishOS test cluster with running VMs and Ceph I/O.
  • Document which tests were passed for each release.
  • A patch that passes the gate is cleared for publication. Do not publish a patch that has failed the gate.

Release and withdrawal

  • Publish approved patches with release notes listing the CVEs covered.
  • Publish the source for every released patch alongside its RPM.
  • If a published patch misbehaves: pull it from the repository, publish an advisory, and give users revert instructions.
  • Maintain the runbook and coverage-gap log.

Secure Boot

  • Manage the Sardina module-signing key and RPM signing key.
  • Document and verify mokutil key enrolment for AlmaLinux users.
  • Work with the Ops team to automate key enrolment on FishOS.

Required skills

  • Linux kernel development: strong C, with hands-on experience backporting kernel patches or debugging kernel modules. Screening will test this directly.
  • Live patching: practical experience with klp-build or kpatch, or demonstrated ability to learn them quickly from source.
  • RPM and the RHEL/AlmaLinux ecosystem: kernel packaging (RPM/SRPM), mock, dnf, createrepo_c and repository metadata.
  • Automation: Python or shell; building and maintaining CI-style pipelines.
  • Signing: GPG key management and RPM signing; kernel module signature verification and MOK enrolment.

- English: working proficiency.

Preferred skills

  • Spoken Russian and/or Mandarin, in addition to English. This is to work closely with Russian- and Mandarin-speaking team members.
  • QEMU-based VM validation or canary testing.
  • Upstream kernel contributions or involvement in the live patching community.
  • Koji or similar build orchestration systems.
  • Ceph I/O testing or storage-heavy workloads.

Key traits

  • Boundary awareness: Willing to say plainly "this CVE needs a reboot" and "this kernel is out of scope" rather than forcing a risky patch
  • Release discipline: Understands that a bad patch is the main reputational risk and will not skip the test gate under pressure
  • Self-directed: Comfortable owning an end-to-end pipeline with minimal supervision
  • Confidentiality: handles embargoed vulnerabilities and unreleased plans with discretion.

Working context

  • Scope: AlmaLinux 10 only, starting with one kernel version.
  • Infrastructure: runs separately from the existing Koji-based OpenStack build infrastructure, but follows the same automation approach.
  • Primary tooling: klp-build, kpatch/kpatch-dnf, mock, createrepo_c, GPG, systemd timers, QEMU and a FishOS test cluster.
  • Release authority: Routine patches are approved by the automated gate; no per-patch sign-off is required. A named release authority reviews weekly summaries, approves exceptions (e.g., a patch that cannot pass the full gate for a documented reason), and handles emergency withdrawals.
  • Backup: one Ops team member is cross-trained on the test gate, publication and withdrawal steps early in the project.

Success Criteria

First milestone

  • klp-build confirmed working on a real Alma 10 kernel
  • End-to-end pipeline producing a signed, tested patch for one CVE class on one kernel version
  • Test gate passed on at least two consecutive builds

- Coverage-gap log and runbook exist

Second milestone

  • Pipeline operating reliably with the test gate on every build
  • Secure Boot enrollment automated on FishOS
  • Sources and tooling published under the appropriate license
  • Runbook and coverage-gap log maintained and current

Working with us

You can work from anywhere in the Asia Pacific region with our remote work setup. We also provide mentoring sessions to support your continuous growth and technical development.

raw.description:
Chief Procurement Officer (CPO) – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Chief Procurement Officer (CPO) is responsible for developing and leading the organization's overall procurement, strategic sourcing, supplier management, purchasing, and procurement governance strategy. The role ensures that procurement activities support organizational objectives, deliver cost efficiencies, strengthen supplier relationships, mitigate procurement risks, and maximize value across the organization.

Within the Insurance & Investments sector, the CPO oversees the procurement of technology, professional services, operational resources, consulting, facilities, outsourced services, and other business-critical goods and services while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements, internal policies, financial controls, and organizational risk frameworks.

The CPO drives strategic sourcing, supplier performance, contract management, procurement transformation, cost optimization, and sustainable procurement practices.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Procurement Strategy & Leadership

  • Develop and implement enterprise-wide procurement strategies aligned with corporate objectives and financial priorities.
  • Establish procurement policies, frameworks, operating models, standards, and governance structures.
  • Lead strategic sourcing, purchasing, procurement operations, and supplier management functions.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize procurement costs, improve purchasing efficiency, and maximize commercial value.
  • Align procurement priorities with business requirements, financial objectives, operational needs, and organizational strategy.

B. Strategic Sourcing & Supplier Selection

  • Lead strategic sourcing activities, supplier identification, market analysis, vendor evaluation, and competitive bidding.
  • Develop sourcing strategies for goods, services, technology, consulting, outsourcing, and business-critical procurement categories.
  • Oversee Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), tendering, supplier negotiations, and procurement decisions.
  • Evaluate suppliers based on cost, quality, service delivery, reliability, risk, innovation, and strategic value.
  • Establish strategic supplier partnerships and long-term commercial relationships.

C. Supplier & Vendor Relationship Management

  • Develop and maintain strategic relationships with key suppliers, vendors, service providers, and business partners.
  • Establish supplier performance management frameworks, service-level agreements (SLAs), and vendor review processes.
  • Monitor supplier performance, delivery quality, pricing, contractual obligations, and service effectiveness.
  • Manage supplier escalations, disputes, performance issues, and relationship risks.
  • Develop supplier diversification, contingency planning, and supplier continuity strategies.

D. Cost Optimization & Financial Management

  • Lead procurement cost optimization, savings initiatives, commercial negotiations, and expenditure management.
  • Develop procurement budgets, financial forecasts, spend plans, and procurement performance targets.
  • Identify cost-saving opportunities, purchasing efficiencies, spend consolidation, and supplier rationalization.
  • Monitor procurement expenditure, contract costs, purchasing trends, and budget performance.
  • Collaborate with Finance to validate savings, track financial benefits, and improve procurement value.
  • Ensure procurement decisions support financial sustainability, profitability, and effective resource allocation.

E. Contract Management & Commercial Negotiation

  • Lead commercial negotiations, procurement contracts, pricing agreements, and strategic vendor arrangements.
  • Establish contract management frameworks, approval processes, commercial controls, and procurement standards.
  • Ensure contracts align with business requirements, financial objectives, risk policies, and legal requirements.
  • Oversee contract renewals, amendments, supplier agreements, procurement terms, and contractual obligations.
  • Coordinate with Legal, Finance, Risk, Compliance, and business stakeholders to manage contract risks.

F. Procurement Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Establish procurement governance frameworks, controls, approval structures, and accountability mechanisms.
  • Ensure procurement activities comply with internal policies, regulatory requirements, financial controls, and corporate governance standards.
  • Identify and mitigate supplier, operational, financial, contractual, reputational, and procurement risks.
  • Oversee procurement audits, documentation, sourcing approvals, supplier due diligence, and procurement transparency.
  • Coordinate with Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit, Legal, and Finance teams.
  • Ensure appropriate oversight of third-party risk, outsourcing arrangements, vendor security, and supplier resilience.

G. Procurement Transformation & Digitalization

  • Lead procurement transformation, modernization, process automation, and digital procurement initiatives.
  • Implement procurement technology, sourcing platforms, contract management systems, spend analytics, and supplier management solutions.
  • Improve procurement processes, workflows, reporting, approvals, and purchasing efficiency.
  • Drive data-driven procurement decision-making through spend analytics, supplier performance data, and procurement KPIs.
  • Promote innovation, operational efficiency, and continuous improvement across procurement activities.

H. Third-Party & Outsourcing Management

  • Oversee procurement and management of third-party providers, outsourced services, consultants, and strategic vendors.
  • Establish third-party risk assessment, supplier onboarding, due diligence, and monitoring frameworks.
  • Evaluate outsourcing arrangements, supplier dependencies, service continuity, and contractual performance.
  • Ensure third-party relationships align with operational resilience, regulatory, security, and business continuity requirements.
  • Manage strategic vendor partnerships and critical supplier relationships.

I. Leadership & Procurement Team Development

  • Lead, develop, and mentor procurement directors, sourcing managers, purchasing teams, contract managers, and procurement professionals.
  • Establish procurement performance expectations, team objectives, competency frameworks, and accountability standards.
  • Build high-performing procurement teams and strengthen organizational procurement capabilities.
  • Develop succession planning, leadership development, and procurement talent strategies.
  • Promote ethical procurement, collaboration, transparency, commercial excellence, and continuous improvement.
